attrs.evidence: A terminology error worth correcting before it is encoded. By Rogers–Roth–Ullman–Vadhan 2016 a privacy FILTER is exactly a stopping rule that prevents exceeding a PRE-SPECIFIED budget; an ODOMETER tracks accumulated loss with no pre-specified budget. A fixed target with a stop is therefore a filter problem, and the filter theorems apply to it. THE REAL GAP IS DIFFERENT and is recorded separately: Feldman–Zrnic 2021 gives a clean adaptive filter at a FIXED RDP order α, and choosing the best α after seeing an adaptive transcript is a data-dependent choice the fixed-α theorem does not justify. That needs a simultaneous/multi-order filter theorem or a precommitment with a union argument — LED-RDP-ORDER.

local_bindings.budget: the pre-specified target the refuted record described

source_assumptions: a budget fixed in advance, for the filter case

attrs.prior_art: Rogers–Roth–Ullman–Vadhan, Privacy Odometers and Filters, 2016 (arXiv:1605.08294) · Feldman–Zrnic 2021 (arXiv:2008.11193) · Whitehouse et al., Fully-Adaptive Composition in Differential Privacy, ICML 2023.
attrs.statement: A stopping rule of the form "halt when convert(spent) exceeds a pre-specified target", with adaptively chosen costs, is an ODOMETER rather than a filter.
